situation: The team must renew the TLS certificate for the internal wiki before it expires next week. The team has renewed it every year using a runbook.

gate.reason: The team asks whether to plan this as a project. The domain tells them to follow the runbook only.

pieces.name: Annual internal certificate renewal
evidence: A written runbook exists and the team ran it successfully for the last three years.
The certificate authority and the install steps have not changed since the last renewal.

second_reading.tipping_condition: The certificate expires before renewal and the wiki goes down for all staff.

pieces.boundary_risk: Complacency. If nobody owns the calendar reminder, the expiry date passes and the problem becomes a crisis.

approach.summary: Follow the runbook. Do not redesign it.
approach.practice: Run the certificate renewal runbook this week and confirm the new expiry date in the browser.

reclassify_triggers: The certificate authority changes its process. Treat the renewal as Complicated until the runbook is updated.
The certificate expires with no replacement. Treat it as Chaotic and restore access first.
